claims.quote: If the application is filed by an agent, the agent must disclose the name of his or her principal(s).
claims.summary: If the application is filed by an agent, the agent must disclose the name of his or her principal(s).

claims.quote: Such documents as may be relevant shall be attached to each application as a part of such application, whether filed electronically or by mail, except that documents previously filed with OFAC may, where appropriate, be incorporated by reference in such application.
claims.summary: Such documents as may be relevant shall be attached to each application, except that documents previously filed with OFAC may be incorporated by reference.

claims.quote: Applicants are encouraged to include, when available, the OFAC Reporting System (ORS) transaction and submission identification numbers.
claims.affected_party: Applicants for the release of blocked funds
claims.summary: Applicants are encouraged to include the OFAC Reporting System (ORS) transaction and submission identification numbers when available.

claims.quote: Applicants may be required to furnish such further information as is deemed necessary to assist OFAC in making a determination.
claims.summary: Applicants may be required to furnish further information as deemed necessary to assist OFAC in making a determination.

claims.quote: Any requests to make such an oral presentation must be submitted via the OFAC License Application Page at https://ofac.treasury.gov/ofac-license-application-page to the attention of the Licensing Division, referencing the relevant Case ID number and a “Request for Oral Presentation.”
claims.affected_party: Applicants or other parties in interest
claims.summary: Requests to make an oral presentation must be submitted via the OFAC License Application Page, referencing the relevant Case ID number and a “Request for Oral Presentation.”

claims.quote: As a condition for the issuance of any specific license, the licensee may be required to file reports with respect to the transactions authorized by the specific license in such form and at such times and places as may be prescribed in the license or otherwise.
claims.summary: As a condition for the issuance of any specific license, the licensee may be required to file reports with respect to the transactions authorized by the specific license.

claims.quote: The denial of a specific license does not preclude the reconsideration of an application or the filing of a further application.
claims.summary: The denial of a specific license does not preclude the reconsideration of an application or the filing of a further application.

claims.quote: The applicant or any other party in interest may at any time request, via the OFAC License Application Page at https://ofac.treasury.gov/ofac-license-application-page , reconsideration of the denial of an application on the basis of new facts or changed circumstances.
claims.affected_party: applicant or any other party in interest
claims.summary: The applicant or any other party in interest may request reconsideration of the denial of an application based on new facts or changed circumstances.

claims.quote: Information submitted to OFAC pursuant to this section will be protected from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552) and the provisions of 31 CFR part 1 if OFAC reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by a FOIA exemption or disclosure is prohibited by law.
claims.affected_party: any party submitting information to OFAC
claims.summary: Information submitted to OFAC pursuant to this section will be protected from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act if OFAC reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by a FOIA exemption or disclosure is prohibited by law.

claims.quote: The Office of Foreign Assets Control will advise each applicant of the decision respecting filed applications.
claims.summary: The Office of Foreign Assets Control will advise each applicant of the decision respecting filed applications.

claims.quote: The provisions of each part of this chapter and any rulings, licenses (whether general or specific), authorizations, instructions, orders, or forms issued thereunder may be amended, modified or revoked at any time.
claims.summary: The provisions of each part of this chapter and any rulings, licenses, authorizations, instructions, orders, or forms issued thereunder may be amended, modified, or revoked at any time.

claims.quote: All rules and other public documents are issued by the Director of the Office of Foreign Assets Control.
claims.summary: All rules and other public documents are issued by the Director of the Office of Foreign Assets Control.

claims.quote: The records of the Office of Foreign Assets Control which are required by the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552) to be made available to the public shall be made available in accordance with the definitions, procedures, payment of fees, and other provisions of the regulations on the Disclosure of Records of the Departmental Offices and of other bureaus and offices of the Department of the Treasury issued under 5 U.S.C. 552 and published at 31 CFR part 1, as well as the provisions of this part.
claims.summary: The records of the Office of Foreign Assets Control which are required by the Freedom of Information Act to be made available to the public shall be made available in accordance with the definitions, procedures, payment of fees, and other provisions of the regulations on the Disclosure of Records.

claims.quote: Records or information obtained or created in the implementation of part 598 of this chapter are not subject to disclosure under section 552(a)(3) of the Freedom of Information Act.
claims.summary: Records or information obtained or created in the implementation of part 598 of this chapter are not subject to disclosure under section 552(a)(3) of the Freedom of Information Act.

claims.quote: The records of the Office of Foreign Assets Control which are required by the Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. 552a) to be made available to an individual shall be made available in accordance with the definitions, procedures, requirements for payment of fees, and other provisions of the Regulations on the Disclosure of Records of the Departmental Offices and of other bureaus and offices of the Department of the Treasury issued under 5.U.S.C. 552a and published at 31 CFR part 1, as well as the provisions of this part.
claims.summary: The Office of Foreign Assets Control must make available records required by the Privacy Act to individuals in accordance with specified regulations and provisions.

claims.quote: OFAC shall make available to the public certain information on a routine basis, not less frequently than monthly, as follows: (i) In each such proceeding against an entity, OFAC shall make available to the public (A) The name and address of the entity involved, (B) The sanctions program involved, (C) A brief description of the violation or alleged violation, (D) A clear indication whether the proceeding resulted in an informal settlement or in the imposition of a penalty, (E) An indication whether the entity voluntarily disclosed the violation or alleged violation to OFAC, and (F) The amount of the penalty imposed or the amount of the agreed settlement.
claims.summary: OFAC must make available to the public certain information on a routine basis, not less frequently than monthly, including details about violations, settlements, and penalties.

claims.quote: In such proceedings against individuals, OFAC shall release on an aggregate basis (A) The number of penalties imposed and informal settlements reached, (B) The sanctions programs involved, (C) A brief description of the violations or alleged violations, (D) A clear indication whether the proceedings resulted in informal settlements, in the imposition of penalties, or in administrative hearing requests pursuant to the Trading With the Enemy Act (TWEA), 50 U.S.C. 5(b), and (E) The amounts of the penalties imposed and the amounts of the agreed settlements.
claims.summary: OFAC must release on an aggregate basis information about proceedings against individuals, including the number of penalties, sanctions programs, and amounts of penalties or settlements.

claims.quote: The medium through which information will be released is OFAC's website at https://ofac.treasury.gov.
claims.summary: OFAC must release information through its website at https://ofac.treasury.gov.

claims.quote: The information made available pursuant to paragraph (d)(1) of this section shall not include the following: (i) The name of any violator or alleged violator who is an individual. (ii) Records or information obtained or created in the implementation of part 598 of this chapter.
claims.summary: OFAC must not include the name of any individual violator or alleged violator and must not include records or information obtained or created in the implementation of part 598 of this chapter in the information made available.

claims.quote: Any person who has blocked and reported to the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) property pursuant to the applicable regulations of this chapter due to mistaken identity or typographical or similar errors, such party may seek to have such property unblocked pursuant to the following administrative procedures:
claims.summary: Any person who has blocked and reported property to OFAC due to mistaken identity or typographical errors may seek to have such property unblocked pursuant to administrative procedures.

claims.quote: Requests to release such property must be sent via email to OFACReport@treasury.gov and include the phrase “31 CFR 501.806—Request for a Compliance Release” in the subject line of the email.
claims.affected_party: party seeking release of blocked property
claims.summary: Requests to release blocked property must be sent via email to OFACReport@treasury.gov with the specified subject line.

claims.quote: A request to release property must include the name, address, telephone number, and email address of the person seeking the release of the property.
claims.affected_party: party seeking release of blocked property
claims.summary: A request to release property must include the name, address, telephone number, and email address of the person seeking the release.

claims.quote: A request to release property should include the following information, where known, concerning the blocked property: (1) The name of the person that holds the blocked property or filed the initial report of blocked property; (2) The actual value, or if unknown, estimated value, in U.S. dollars of the blocked property, as included in the initial report of blocked property; (3) The date of the blocking included in the initial report of blocked property; (4) A copy of a valid government-issued identification document, social security number or employer identification number for a person whose property is believed to have been blocked in error, when applicable; (5) The OFAC Reporting System (ORS) identification numbers associated with the initial report of blocked property filed with OF, when available; (6) A description of the property or underlying transaction; and (7) A narrative description of the reasons why the applicant believes the property was blocked in error.
claims.affected_party: party seeking release of blocked property
claims.summary: A request to release property should include specific information about the blocked property, including name, value, date of blocking, identification documents, ORS numbers, description, and reasons for the error.

claims.quote: Upon receipt of the materials required by paragraph (d) of this section, OFAC may request additional material, if available, from the applicant concerning the blocked property pursuant to § 501.602.
claims.affected_party: party seeking release of blocked property
claims.summary: OFAC may request additional material from the applicant concerning the blocked property pursuant to § 501.602.

claims.quote: Following review of all applicable submissions, OFAC will determine whether the property should be released. In the event that OFAC determines that the property should be released, it will direct the person to release the property to the appropriate party.
claims.affected_party: party seeking release of blocked property
claims.summary: OFAC will determine whether the property should be released and will direct the person to release the property to the appropriate party.

claims.quote: A person may submit a petition for administrative reconsideration pursuant to the procedures outlined below in order to seek removal of a person or property (e.g., a vessel) from the List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List) or any other list or identification of sanctioned persons or property maintained by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC):
claims.summary: A person may submit a petition for administrative reconsideration to seek removal of a person or property from the SDN List or any other list of sanctioned persons or property maintained by OFAC.

claims.quote: This submission must be made via email to OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov.
claims.summary: The submission must be made via email to OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov.

claims.quote: The information submitted by the person seeking removal of a person or property from the SDN List or any other list or identification of sanctioned persons or property maintained by OF, will be reviewed by OFAC, which may request clarifying, corroborating, or other additional information.
claims.summary: The information submitted by the person seeking removal of a person or property from the SDN List or any other list or identification of sanctioned persons or property maintained by OFAC will be reviewed by OFAC, which may request clarifying, corroborating, or other additional information.

claims.quote: A person seeking removal of a person or property from the SDN List or any other list or identification of sanctioned persons or property maintained by OFAC may request a meeting with OFAC; however, such meetings are not required, and the office may, at its discretion, decline to conduct such meetings prior to completing a review pursuant to this section.
claims.summary: A person seeking removal of a person or property from the SDN List or any other list or identification of sanctioned persons or property maintained by OFAC may request a meeting with OFAC; however, such meetings are not required, and the office may, at its discretion, decline to conduct such meetings prior to completing a review pursuant to this section.

claims.quote: After OFAC has conducted a review of the request for reconsideration, it will provide a written decision to the person seeking the removal of a person or property from the SDN List or any other list or identification of sanctioned persons or property maintained by OFAC.
claims.summary: After OFAC has conducted a review of the request for reconsideration, it will provide a written decision to the person seeking the removal of a person or property from the SDN List or any other list or identification of sanctioned persons or property maintained by OFAC.

claims.quote: The information collection requirements in subparts C and D have been approved by the Office of Management and Budget (“OMB”) under the Paperwork Reduction Act (44 U.S.C. 3507(j)) and assigned control number 1505-0164. An agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless it displays a valid control number assigned by OMB.
claims.summary: The information collection requirements in subparts C and D have been approved by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) under the Paperwork Reduction Act and assigned control number 1505-0164. A person is not required to respond to a collection of information unless it displays a valid control number assigned by OMB.

claims.quote: Notification to OFAC of an apparent violation is not a voluntary self-disclosure if: a third party is required to and does notify OFAC of the apparent violation or a substantially similar apparent violation because a transaction was blocked or rejected by that third party (regardless of when OFAC receives such notice from the third party and regardless of whether the Subject Person was aware of the third party's disclosure); the disclosure includes false or misleading information; the disclosure (when considered along with supplemental information provided by the Subject Person) is materially incomplete; the disclosure is not self-initiated (including when the disclosure results from a suggestion or order of a federal or state agency or official); or, when the Subject Person is an entity, the disclosure is made by an individual in a Subject Person entity without the authorization of the entity's senior management.
claims.summary: Notification to OFAC of an apparent violation is not a voluntary self-disclosure under certain conditions.

claims.quote: Responding to an administrative subpoena or other inquiry from, or filing a license application with, OFAC is not a voluntary self-disclosure.
claims.summary: Responding to an administrative subpoena or filing a license application with OFAC is not considered a voluntary self-disclosure.

claims.quote: In addition to notification, a voluntary self-disclosure must include, or be followed within a reasonable period of time by, a report of sufficient detail to afford a complete understanding of an apparent violation's circumstances, and should also be followed by responsiveness to any follow-up inquiries by OFAC.
claims.summary: A voluntary self-disclosure must include a detailed report and responsiveness to follow-up inquiries by OFAC.

claims.quote: If OFAC determines that there is insufficient evidence to conclude that a violation has occurred and/or, based on an analysis of the General Factors outlined in Section III of these Guidelines, concludes that the conduct does not rise to a level warranting an administrative response, then no action will be taken.
claims.summary: OFAC must determine whether there is sufficient evidence to conclude a violation has occurred before taking action.

claims.quote: If OFAC is aware that the Subject Person has knowledge of OFAC's investigation, OFAC generally will issue a letter to the Subject Person indicating that the investigation is being closed with no administrative action being taken.
claims.summary: OFAC must issue a letter to the Subject Person if the investigation is closed with no administrative action.

claims.quote: If OFAC determines that additional information regarding the apparent violation is needed, it may request further information from the Subject Person or third parties, including through an administrative subpoena issued pursuant to 31 CFR 501.602.
claims.summary: OFAC must request additional information from the Subject Person or third parties if needed.

claims.quote: In the case of an institution subject to regulation where OFAC has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Subject Person's regulator, OFAC will follow the procedures set forth in such MOU regarding consultation with the regulator.
claims.summary: OFAC must follow procedures outlined in the MOU when consulting with the regulator.

claims.quote: Even in the absence of an MOU, OFAC may seek relevant information about a regulated institution and/or the conduct constituting the apparent violation from the institution's federal, state, or foreign regulator.
claims.summary: OFAC may seek relevant information from the institution's regulators even without an MOU.

claims.quote: Upon receipt of information determined to be sufficient to assess the apparent violation, OFAC will decide, based on an analysis of the General Factors outlined in Section III of these Guidelines, whether to pursue further enforcement action or whether some other response to the apparent violation is appropriate.
claims.summary: OFAC must decide whether to pursue further enforcement action or another response to the apparent violation based on an analysis of the General Factors.

claims.quote: OFAC may issue a cautionary letter, which may convey OFAC's concerns about the underlying conduct and/or the Subject Person's OFAC compliance policies, practices and/or procedures.
claims.summary: OFAC may issue a cautionary letter to convey concerns about the underlying conduct and/or the Subject Person's compliance policies, practices, and procedures.

claims.quote: A Finding of Violation represents a final enforcement response to the violation, unless OFAC later learns of additional related violations or other relevant facts, and constitutes a final agency determination that a violation has occurred.
claims.summary: A Finding of Violation constitutes a final agency determination that a violation has occurred, unless OF,AC later learns of additional related violations or other relevant facts.

claims.quote: The imposition of a civil monetary penalty constitutes a final agency determination that a violation has occurred and represents a final civil enforcement response to the violation.
claims.summary: The imposition of a civil monetary penalty constitutes a final agency determination that a violation has occurred and represents a final civil enforcement response to the violation.

claims.quote: OFAC will afford the Subject Person an opportunity to respond to OFAC's determination that a violation has occurred before a final penalty is imposed.
claims.summary: OFAC must afford the Subject Person an opportunity to respond to OFAC's determination that a violation has occurred before a final penalty is imposed.

claims.quote: In appropriate circumstances, OFAC may refer the matter to appropriate law enforcement agencies for criminal investigation and/or prosecution.
claims.summary: OFAC may refer the matter to appropriate law enforcement agencies for criminal investigation and/or prosecution in appropriate circumstances.

claims.quote: OFAC may also take the following administrative actions in response to an apparent violation: 1. License Denial, Suspension, Modification, or Revocation.
claims.summary: OFAC may take administrative actions such as License Denial, Suspension, Modification, or Revocation in response to an apparent violation.

claims.quote: OFAC authorizations to engage in a transaction (including the release of blocked funds) pursuant to a general or specific license may be withheld, denied, suspended, modified, or revoked in response to an apparent violation.
claims.summary: OFAC may withhold, deny, suspend, modify, or revoke authorizations in response to an apparent violation.

claims.quote: OFAC may order the Subject Person to cease and desist from conduct that is prohibited by any of the sanctions programs enforced by OFAC when OFAC has reason to believe that a Subject Person has engaged in such conduct and/or that such conduct is ongoing or may recur.
claims.summary: OFAC may order the Subject Person to cease and desist from prohibited conduct if such conduct is ongoing or may recur.

claims.quote: Among the factors OFAC may consider in evaluating willfulness or recklessness are: 1. Willfulness. Was the conduct at issue the result of a decision to take action with the knowledge that such action would constitute a violation of U.S. law? Did the Subject Person know that the underlying conduct constituted, or likely constituted, a violation of U.S. law at the time of the conduct?
claims.summary: OFAC may consider whether the Subject Person knew that the conduct constituted a violation of U.S. law.

claims.quote: Among the factors OFAC may consider in evaluating willfulness or recklessness are: 2. Recklessness. Did the Subject Person demonstrate reckless disregard for U.S. sanctions requirements or otherwise fail to exercise a minimal degree of caution or care in avoiding conduct that led to the apparent violation? Were there warning signs that should have alerted the Subject Person that an action or failure to act would lead to an apparent violation?
claims.summary: OFAC may consider whether the Subject Person demonstrated reckless disregard for U.S. sanctions requirements or failed to exercise caution.

claims.quote: Among the factors OFAC may consider in evaluating willfulness or recklessness are: 3. Concealment. Was there an effort by the Subject Person to hide or purposely obfuscate its conduct in order to mislead OFAC, Federal, State, or foreign regulators, or other parties involved in the conduct about an apparent violation?
claims.summary: OFAC may consider whether the Subject Person attempted to conceal its conduct to mislead regulators.

claims.quote: Among the factors OFAC may consider in evaluating willfulness or recklessness are: 4. Pattern of Conduct. Did the apparent violation constitute or result from a pattern or practice of conduct or was it relatively isolated and atypical in nature?
claims.summary: OFAC may consider whether the apparent violation resulted from a pattern or practice of conduct.

claims.quote: Among the factors OFAC may consider in evaluating willfulness or recklessness are: 5. Prior Notice. Was the Subject Person on notice, or should it reasonably have been on notice, that the conduct at issue, or similar conduct, constituted a violation of U.S. law?
claims.summary: OFAC may consider whether the Subject Person was on notice or should have been on notice that the conduct constituted a violation of U.S. law.

claims.quote: Among the factors OFAC may consider in evaluating willfulness or recklessness are: 6. Management Involvement. In cases of entities, at what level within the organization did the willful or reckless conduct occur? Were supervisory or managerial level staff aware, or should they reasonably have been aware, of the willful or reckless conduct?
claims.summary: OFAC may consider the level of management involvement in willful or reckless conduct.

claims.quote: Among the factors OFAC may consider in evaluating the Subject Person's awareness of the conduct at issue are: 1. Actual Knowledge. Did the Subject Person have actual knowledge that the conduct giving rise to an apparent violation took place?
claims.summary: OFAC may consider whether the Subject Person had actual knowledge of the conduct giving rise to an apparent violation.

claims.quote: OFAC will only consider a Subject Person's sanctions history for the five years preceding the date of the transaction giving rise to the apparent violation.
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report sanctions history for the five years preceding the date of the transaction giving rise to the apparent violation.

claims.quote: OFAC will follow the procedures set forth in such MOU regarding consultation with the regulator with regard to the quality and effectiveness of the Subject Person's compliance program.
claims.summary: A Subject Person must follow the procedures set forth in the MOU regarding consultation with the regulator concerning the quality and effectiveness of their compliance program.

claims.quote: OFAC may take into consideration the views of federal, state, or foreign regulators, where relevant.
claims.summary: A Subject Person must take into consideration the views of federal, state, or foreign regulators, where relevant.

claims.quote: Among the factors OFAC may consider in evaluating the remedial response are: 1. The steps taken by the Subject Person upon learning of the apparent violation. Did the Subject Person immediately stop the conduct at issue?
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report the steps taken upon learning of the apparent violation, including whether they immediately stopped the conduct at issue.

claims.quote: Did the Subject Person discover necessary information to ascertain the causes and extent of the apparent violation, fully and expeditiously? Was senior management fully informed? If so, when?
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report whether they discovered necessary information to ascertain the causes and extent of the apparent violation, fully and expeditiously, and whether senior management was fully informed.

claims.quote: Did the Subject Person adopt new and more effective internal controls and procedures to prevent a recurrence of the apparent violation?
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report whether they adopted new and more effective internal controls and procedures to prevent a recurrence of the apparent violation.

claims.quote: Did the entity provide the individual(s) responsible for the apparent violation with additional training, and/or take other appropriate action, to ensure that similar violations do not occur in the future?
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report whether they provided the individual(s) responsible for the apparent violation with additional training and/or took other appropriate action to ensure similar violations do not occur in the future.

claims.quote: Where applicable, whether the Subject Person undertook a thorough review to identify other possible violations.
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report whether they undertook a thorough review to identify other possible violations.

claims.quote: Among the factors OFAC may consider in evaluating cooperation with OFAC are: 1. Did the Subject Person voluntarily self-disclose the apparent violation to OFAC?
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report whether they voluntarily self-disclosed the apparent violation to OFAC.

claims.quote: Did the Subject Person provide OFAC with all relevant information regarding an apparent violation (whether or not voluntarily self-disclosed)?
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report whether they provided OFAC with all relevant information regarding an apparent violation.

claims.quote: Did the Subject Person research and disclose to OFAC relevant information regarding any other apparent violations caused by the same course of conduct?
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report whether they researched and disclosed to OFAC relevant information regarding any other apparent violations caused by the same course of conduct.

claims.quote: Did the Subject Person cooperate with, and promptly respond to, all requests for information?
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report whether they cooperated with and promptly responded to all requests for information.

claims.quote: Did the Subject Person enter into a statute of limitations tolling agreement, if requested by OFAC?
claims.summary: A Subject Person must report whether they entered into a statute of limitations tolling agreement, if requested by OFAC.

claims.quote: the timing of the apparent violation in relation to the adoption of the applicable prohibitions, particularly if the apparent violation took place immediately after relevant changes in the sanctions program regulations or the addition of a new name to OFAC's List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List).
claims.summary: The timing of the apparent violation in relation to the adoption of the applicable prohibitions, particularly if the apparent violation took place immediately after relevant changes in the sanctions program regulations or the addition of a new name to OFAC's List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List).

claims.quote: other enforcement actions taken by federal, state, or local agencies against the Subject Person for the apparent violation or similar apparent violations, including whether the settlement of alleged violations of OFAC regulations is part of a comprehensive settlement with other federal, state, or local agencies.
claims.summary: Other enforcement actions taken by federal, state, or local agencies against the Subject Person for the apparent violation or similar apparent violations, including whether the settlement of alleged violations of OFAC regulations is part of a comprehensive settlement with other federal, state, or local agencies.

claims.quote: the impact administrative action may have on promoting future compliance with U.S. economic sanctions by the Subject Person and similar Subject Persons, particularly those in the same industry sector.
claims.summary: The impact administrative action may have on promoting future compliance with U.S. economic sanctions by the Subject Person and similar Subject Persons, particularly those in the same industry sector.

claims.quote: the failure to comply with a requirement to furnish information pursuant to 31 CFR 501.602 may result in a penalty in an amount up to $29,150, irrespective of whether any other violation is alleged.
claims.summary: The failure to comply with a requirement to furnish information pursuant to 3.1 CFR 501.602 may result in a penalty in an amount up to $29,150, irrespective of whether any other violation is alleged.

claims.quote: Where OFAC has reason to believe that the apparent violation(s) that is the subject of the requirement to furnish information involves a transaction(s) valued at greater than $500,000, a failure to comply with a requirement to furnish information may result in a penalty in an amount up to $72,876, irrespective of whether any other violation is alleged.
claims.summary: Where OFAC has reason to believe that the apparent violation(s) that is the subject of the requirement to furnish information involves a transaction(s) valued at greater than $500,000, a failure to comply with a requirement to furnish information may result in a penalty in an amount up to $72,876, irrespective of whether any other violation is alleged.

claims.quote: A failure to comply with a requirement to furnish information may be considered a continuing violation, and the penalties described above may be imposed each month that a party has continued to fail to comply with the requirement to furnish information.
claims.summary: A failure to comply with a requirement to furnish information may be considered a continuing violation, and the penalties described above may be imposed each month that a party has continued to fail to comply with the requirement to furnish information.

claims.quote: The late filing of a required report, whether set forth in regulations or in a specific license, may result in a civil monetary penalty in an amount up to $3,550, if filed within the first 30 days after the report is due, and a penalty in an amount up to $7,104 if filed more than 30 days after the report is due.
claims.summary: The late filing of a required report, whether set forth in regulations or in a specific license, may result in a civil monetary penalty in an amount up to $3,550, if filed within the first 30 days after the report is due, and a penalty in an amount up to $7,104 if filed more than 30 days after the report is due.

claims.quote: If the report relates to blocked assets, the penalty may include an additional $1,422 for every 30 days that the report is overdue, up to 10 years.
claims.summary: If the report relates to blocked assets, the penalty may include an additional $1,422 for every 30 days that the report is overdue, up to 10 years.

claims.quote: If OFAC has reason to believe that a sanctions violation has occurred and believes that a civil monetary penalty is appropriate, it will issue a Pre-Penalty Notice in accordance with the procedures set forth in the particular regulations governing the conduct giving rise to the apparent violation.
claims.summary: OFAC must issue a Pre-Penalty Notice if it believes a sanctions violation has occurred and a civil monetary penalty is appropriate.

claims.quote: The amount of the proposed penalty set forth in the Pre-Penalty Notice will reflect OFAC's preliminary assessment of the appropriate penalty amount, based on information then in OFAC's possession.
claims.summary: OFAC must set the proposed penalty amount based on its preliminary assessment of the appropriate penalty amount.

claims.quote: If, after issuance of a Pre-Penalty Notice, OFAC determines that a penalty in an amount that represents an increase of more than 10 percent from the proposed penalty set forth in the Pre-Penalty Notice is appropriate, or if OFAC intends to allege additional violations, it will issue a revised Pre-Penalty Notice setting forth the new proposed penalty amount and/or alleged violations.
claims.summary: OFAC must issue a revised Pre-Penalty Notice if it determines that a penalty increase of more than 10 percent is appropriate or if it intends to allege additional violations.

claims.quote: The Pre-Penalty Notice will set forth the following with respect to the specific violations alleged and the proposed penalties: i. Description of the alleged violations, including the number of violations and their value, for which a penalty is being proposed; ii. Identification of the regulatory or other provisions alleged to have been violated; iii. Identification of the base category (defined below) according to which the proposed penalty amount was calculated and the General Factors that were most relevant to the determination of the proposed penalty amount; iv. The maximum amount of the penalty to which the Subject Person could be subject under applicable law; and v. The proposed penalty amount, determined in accordance with the provisions set forth in these Guidelines.
claims.summary: OFAC must set forth specific details about the alleged violations and proposed penalties in the Pre-Penalty Notice.

claims.quote: The Pre-Penalty Notice will also include information regarding how to respond to the Pre-Penalty Notice including: i. A statement that the Subject Person may submit a written response to the Pre-Penalty Notice by a date certain addressing the alleged violation(s), the General Factors Affecting Administrative Action set forth in Section III of these Guidelines, and any other information or evidence that the Subject Person deems relevant to OFAC's consideration. ii. A statement that a failure to respond to the Pre-Penalty Notice may result in the imposition of a civil monetary penalty.
claims.summary: OFAC must include information on how to respond to the Pre-Penalty Notice, including the consequences of failing to respond.

claims.quote: A Subject Person may submit a written response to the Pre-Penalty Notice in accordance with the procedures set forth in the particular regulations governing the conduct giving rise to the apparent violation.
claims.summary: A Subject Person must submit a written response to the Pre-Penalty Notice in accordance with the procedures set forth in the regulations.

claims.quote: Generally, the response should either agree to the proposed penalty set forth in the Pre-Penalty Notice or set forth reasons why a penalty should not be imposed or, if imposed, why it should be a lesser amount than proposed, with particular attention paid to the General Factors Affecting Administrative Action set forth in Section III of these Guidelines.
claims.summary: A Subject Person must either agree to the proposed penalty or provide reasons why a penalty should not be imposed or should be a lesser amount, with attention to the General Factors.

claims.quote: The response should include all documentary or other evidence available to the Subject Person that supports the arguments set forth in the response.
claims.summary: A Subject Person must include all documentary or other evidence available to support the arguments in their response.

claims.quote: If OFAC receives no response to a Pre-Penalty Notice within the time prescribed in the Pre-Penalty Notice, or if following the receipt of a response to a Pre-Penalty Notice and a review of the information and evidence contained therein OFAC concludes that a civil monetary penalty is warranted, a Penalty Notice generally will be issued in accordance with the procedures set forth in the particular regulations governing the conduct giving rise to the violation.
claims.summary: OFAC must issue a Penalty Notice if no response is received within the prescribed time or if it concludes that a civil monetary penalty is warranted.

claims.quote: A Penalty Notice constitutes a final agency determination that a violation has occurred.
claims.summary: A Penalty Notice constitutes a final agency determination that a violation has occurred.

claims.quote: The penalty amount set forth in the Penalty Notice will take into account relevant additional information provided in response to a Pre-Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: OFAC must take into account relevant additional information provided in response to a Pre-Penalty Notice when setting the penalty amount.

claims.quote: In the absence of a response to a Pre-Penalty Notice, the penalty amount set forth in the Penalty Notice will generally be the same as the proposed penalty set forth in the Pre-Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: If there is no response to a Pre-Penalty Notice, the penalty amount in the Penalty Notice will generally match the proposed penalty in the Pre-Penalty Notice.

claims.quote: The imposition of a civil monetary penalty pursuant to a Penalty Notice creates a debt due the U.S. Government.
claims.summary: The imposition of a civil monetary penalty creates a debt due to the U.S. Government.

claims.quote: OFAC will advise Treasury's Financial Management Division upon the imposition of a penalty.
claims.summary: OFAC must advise Treasury's Financial Management Division upon the imposition of a penalty.

claims.quote: The Financial Management Division may take follow-up action to collect the penalty assessed if it is not paid within the prescribed time period set forth in the Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: The Financial Management Division may take follow-up action to collect the penalty if it is not paid within the prescribed time period.

claims.quote: In addition or instead, the matter may be referred to the U.S. Department of Justice for appropriate action to recover the penalty.
claims.summary: The matter may be referred to the U.S. Department of Justice for appropriate action to recover the penalty.

claims.quote: The issuance of a Penalty Notice constitutes final agency action with respect to the violation(s) for which the penalty is assessed.
claims.summary: The issuance of a Penalty Notice constitutes final agency action with respect to the violation(s) for which the penalty is assessed.

claims.quote: The penalty amount proposed in a Pre-Penalty Notice shall generally be calculated as follows, except that neither the base amount nor the proposed penalty will exceed the applicable statutory maximum amount:
claims.summary: The penalty amount proposed in a Pre-Penalty Notice shall generally be calculated as follows, with the base amount and proposed penalty not exceeding the applicable statutory maximum amount.

claims.quote: For apparent violations identified in the Cuba Penalty Schedule, 68 Fed. Reg. 4429 (Jan. 29, 2003), for which a civil monetary penalty has been deemed appropriate, the base penalty amount shall equal the amount set forth in the Schedule for such violation, except that the base penalty amount shall be reduced by 50% in cases of voluntary self-disclosure.
claims.summary: For apparent violations identified in the Cuba Penalty Schedule, the base penalty amount shall equal the amount set forth in the Schedule for such violation, except that the base penalty amount shall be reduced by 50% in cases of voluntary self-disclosure.

claims.quote: In a non-egregious case, if the apparent violation is disclosed through a voluntary self-disclosure by the Subject Person, the base amount of the proposed civil penalty in the Pre-Penalty Notice shall be one-half of the transaction value, capped at a maximum base amount of $188,850 per violation, except where the statutory maximum penalty applicable to the apparent violation is less than $377,700, in which case the base amount of the proposed civil penalty in the Pre-Penalty Notice shall be capped at one-half the statutory maximum penalty applicable to the apparent violation.
claims.summary: In a non-egregious case, if the apparent violation is disclosed through a voluntary self-disclosure by the Subject Person, the base amount of the proposed civil penalty in the Pre-Penalty Notice shall be one-half of the transaction value, capped at a maximum base amount of $188,850 per violation, except where the statutory maximum penalty applicable to the apparent violation is less than $377,700.

claims.quote: In a non-egregious case, if the apparent violation comes to OFAC's attention by means other than a voluntary self-disclosure, the base amount of the proposed civil penalty in the Pre-Penalty Notice shall be the 'applicable schedule amount,' as defined above.
claims.summary: In a non-egregious case, if the apparent violation comes to OFAC's attention by means other than a voluntary self-disclosure, the base amount of the proposed civil penalty in the Pre-Penalty Notice shall be the 'applicable schedule amount,' as defined above.

claims.quote: In an egregious case, if the apparent violation is disclosed through a voluntary self-disclosure by a Subject Person, the base amount of the proposed civil penalty in the Pre-Penalty Notice shall be one-half of the applicable statutory maximum penalty applicable to the violation.
claims.summary: A Subject Person must disclose an apparent violation through a voluntary self-disclosure to receive a reduced civil penalty.

claims.quote: In an egregious case, if the apparent violation comes to OFAC's attention by means other than a voluntary self-disclosure, the base amount of the proposed civil penalty in the Pre-Penalty Notice shall be the applicable statutory maximum penalty amount applicable to the violation.
claims.summary: If an apparent violation comes to OFAC's attention without a voluntary self-disclosure, the base civil penalty shall be the statutory maximum penalty.

claims.quote: The civil penalty amounts authorized under these statutes are subject to adjustment pursuant to the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act of 1990 (Pub. L. 101-410, as amended, 28 U.S.C. 2461 note).
claims.summary: Civil penalty amounts are subject to adjustment under the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act.
